market_holds: No usable option chain: the baseline found the ATM legs one-sided, so there is no implied move. My own arithmetic on Yahoo hourly bars gives the stock's move at about 13:00 ET on its last four print days: Nov-2025 (Q3'25) about -7%, Feb-2026 (Q4'25) about +20%, May-2026 (Q1'26) about +15% (closed only +2.5%), Aug-2026 (Q2'26) about +2-3% (opened +8%, closed +0.3%). So the usual 13:00 move is about 7-15%, and the last three prints all opened up 8-13% and then faded. Consensus from Yahoo earningsTrend, fetched 2026-11-17 (n=4): Q3 revenue $57.48M, the exact midpoint of the $55-60M guide; EPS $0.05 (0.06 ninety days ago). Q4 revenue $62.52M (+6.1% y/y on Q4'25 $58.9M); Q4 EPS $0.13, down from $0.16 ninety days ago. FY26 revenue $223.77M (+7.5%, the low end of management's 'high single digit'). Consensus H2 is $120.0M against management's own framing of H2 about 15% above H1 ($103.8M x 1.15 = $119.4M), so the Street sits right on the guide. Run-in: -5.0% over 5 days and -5.5% over 20 days, against IWM -3.9% / -2.3% and SPY -2.5% / -4.9%. Most of it is the tape: KRNT barely reacted to Gildan's 25% fall on 2026-11-05 (-3.4% on a day SPY fell 4.4%). Short interest is 1.73% of float as of 2026-10-30 (Yahoo), so not crowded. Mean target $25 from 4 analysts; last actions were Needham Buy with target to $23 and Morgan Stanley Equal-Weight with target to $19, both 2026-08-12/13. Cash about $451M against a market cap of roughly $0.7B.
view: This print will turn on the Q4 guide set against the $62.5M Q4 consensus, not on Q3 revenue. Kornit has landed at or above the top of its range two quarters running: Q1 $48.5M vs $45-49M, Q2 $55.3M vs $51-55M, a 4-4.6% surprise on the aggregators. So a Q3 near $59-60M against a $57.5M consensus is the base case and probably the market's whisper. The same quarter a year ago is the warning. In Nov-2025 Kornit beat Q3, guided Q4 to $56-60M (read as a y/y decline) and the stock was about -7% at 13:00. This year the arithmetic is tight in the same way. If Q3 comes in at $59.5M, management's 'H2 about 15% over H1' implies a Q4 of about $59.9M, and FY +8% implies about $61.6M. Both are below the $62.5M consensus, so a beat-and-hold guide can still read as a soft Q4. Since the August call the counterparty evidence has split. Gildan's wholesale/printwear channel fell 10.8% pro forma in Q3, with distributors cutting replenishment, and full-year guidance was cut to $5.4-5.5B on 2026-11-05. That is a negative read for the screen-printer and long-tail base, where Kornit sells about 60% of its systems and already admitted 'long tail customers declining'. Cimpress grew 2% organic. Etsy, by contrast, had marketplace GMS +8.8% in Q3 and guided Q4 GMS +5-7%, which is healthy for the online print-on-demand channel where Kornit's strategic accounts sit. Management also said in August that Q3 and Q4 orders were already in hand and strategic-customer upgrades continue through H2. FX has turned mildly helpful: USD/ILS averaged 3.025 in Q3 vs 2.946 in Q2, and about 3.16 quarter-to-date in Q4 (3.25 now). That helps the EBITDA guide on shekel opex and partly reverses the reason Q4 EPS estimates were cut from $0.16 to $0.13. The positives (a beat habit, ARR momentum the market has rewarded at the open three times, a tape-driven pullback, a cash floor) and the negatives (a weakening decorated-apparel channel and a Q4 consensus that sits above management's own H2 arithmetic) roughly offset. The opening gaps have also faded by 13:00 on two of the last three prints. I see a large two-sided move and no direction I can stand behind.

recommendation.reason: Two mechanisms are visible and they point opposite ways, and neither has evidence I can show is missing from the price. On one side, Kornit's habit of beating the top of its guide against a midpoint consensus, plus a mild FX tailwind. On the other, a Q4 consensus ($62.5M) above what management's own H2 framing implies once Q3 beats, plus Gildan's printwear-channel weakness since the last call. Below 65% either way, so no trade.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The Q4 revenue guide midpoint. At $63M or more with ARR above $38M I would lean long; at $60M or less (the H2-15% arithmetic), or with any comment that the long tail or screen-printer demand worsened in Q3, I would lean short.

self_critique: The strongest case for long: the last three prints opened up 8-13% on AIC/ARR momentum, the stock has been dragged 9% off its October high by the tape and not by its own news, the Q3 consensus sits at the midpoint against a top-end beat habit, and the shekel has turned. The market has under-anchored this name's results three times running. The strongest case for short: Gildan's channel collapse is fresh, unbudgeted evidence for the screen-printer base, and the Q4 consensus needs more than management's own H2 framing gives. Both are real, so I stay near 50.
